guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul / Jackson Randy Rhoads model / Gibson Les Paul (Wylde "Bullseye")
guitar.evidence: Randy Rhoads played Gibson Les Pauls and the Karl Sandoval-built polka-dot V (later Jackson's signature Randy Rhoads model) on "Crazy Train"/"Mr. Crowley"; Zakk Wylde's bullseye Gibson Les Paul is iconic for "Bark at the Moon"-era and beyond.
guitar.notes: Was unknown despite Ozzy's guitarists being among the most documented in metal history; filled with high confidence.

tone.target: sustainy 80s lead with long delay and reverb
tone.profile: sustainy 80s lead with long delay and reverb
tone.summary: A polished, sustained lead tone utilizing a British-style amp (UK SLP) combined with chorus/delay for an expansive, shimmering 80s sound.

rig.name: Ozzy Osbourne - Mr. Crowley - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up high-gain sustain and ambient noise.
Provide subtle boost and smooth the initial signal for singing sustain.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used to simulate a clean, transparent pre-amp lift rather than a specific OD pedal.

blocks.purpose: Add the characteristic '80s sheen' and width to the lead tone.
Provide smooth, singing lead gain without heavy crunch or fuzz.
blocks.gap: Red Haze is chosen for its smoother character compared to pure distortion models.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic British 80s lead amp sound (Marshall-esque).
Slight mid-push and overall polish to enhance the lead tone.
Achieve the required long, ambient delay for space and sustain.
Add the required prominent plate/hall reverb for an expansive 80s sound.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR to better capture the polished, ambient sound required for 80s lead tones.

proposals.reason: Enhance the polished, spacious 80s sheen and sustain.
